name: primary-iso3-gap
definition: For every GDACS-sourced future, whether the raw feed's top-level singular `properties.iso3` (the event's current/reporting-position country) is a member of the future's committed `iso3` array, which practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py (gdacs_futures, lines 48-50) builds only from `properties.affectedcountries`. obs-2026-08-09-1.json found six tropical-cyclone futures in both preserved GDACS snapshots (2026-08-08 and 2026-08-09) where the top-level iso3 is absent from affectedcountries and therefore absent from the future's iso3 array, even though the same country is named in the future's own `where` text. A purely mechanical field-membership check against already-preserved raw snapshot bytes — no judgement about which country is 'really' affected.
test_rule: On each nightly notary run, after gdacs_futures() extracts the night's features, for every ALERT_EPISODE future compare its committed iso3 list to the raw snapshot feature's top-level properties.iso3 for the same event id. If properties.iso3 is non-empty and not present in the future's iso3 array, record {future_id, dropped_iso3} in that night's run summary under primary_iso3_dropped. The sensor fires (is worth a note) on any run where the list is non-empty, since a coverage gap in a country field does not need a threshold or multiple nights to be a real gap — unlike sensor-fts-country-coverage, which measures a rate that needs a baseline before a change means anything.
falsification: Falsified as a live sensor once the underlying code is fixed (reading affectedcountries union the top-level iso3, or an equivalent correction) and primary_iso3_dropped stays empty for many subsequent nights purely because the bug is gone — at that point the sensor has done its one job and should be retired, not kept running for a case that can no longer occur. Also scoped, not general: NHC-sourced futures never carry affectedcountries or a comparable top-level/list split (practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py, nhc_futures, line 75 sets iso3 to [] unconditionally), so this sensor only ever applies to GDACS-sourced futures and would need a different check, not a wider threshold, if NHC's schema changes.

promotion.settles: a debt named by the machine's own obs-2026-08-10-2.json: the check had already run as code in every run.json since commit 79f8a02 (2026-08-09T14:50:39+00:00), with the run.py comment naming this proposal directly, but no promotion or review block had ever been written into this file.
promotion.test_rule_held: foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-12/run.json is the first run.json to exist since the fix commit (the anchor deadlock, obs-2026-08-11-1.json/obs-2026-08-12-1.json, blocked every run from 2026-08-09T14:50 until tonight) and it shows primary_iso3_dropped: [] -- exactly what the test rule expects once the six affected futures were corrected by hand (autonomy/log.jsonl step foreknown-correct-primary-iso3, 2026-08-09T14:50:39+00:00). The check ran, found nothing, and said so in the record, which is what 'held' means for a check whose own falsification clause is an eventual empty list.
promotion.kept_unchanged: definition, test_rule and falsification are the machine's text and match the running code as written; the guard still fires unconditionally on any non-empty list, no threshold added.
